Definition: Does the government maintain a digital address register?
Comments: Searched for a national address registry (official address database, unique address identifier, postal addressing system) for Senegal; did not find authoritative evidence of an operational national address registry in sources reviewed.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light check surfaced two independent, clearly authoritative sources (a Paris School of Economics/DGID/World Bank-backed property-tax digitisation project, and a peer-reviewed paper by Senegalese computer scientists) both stating explicitly that Senegal lacks a harmonised/official street-level addressing system. Per protocol this moved the row from the fast path to the full path. Score changed from 0/Unknown to 1/No: a formal national address register does not exist, though adjacent systems (NICAD cadastral parcel IDs since 2012, 5-digit postal codes since 2015) provide partial locality/parcel identification.
revised_comments: Senegal does not maintain a harmonised national address register recording standardised street names, numbers and postal addresses for buildings and plots. Existing tools — the NICAD cadastral identification number (introduced 2012) and 5-digit postal codes (introduced 2015) — provide parcel- and locality-level identifiers rather than street-level addressing. Research on Dakar's property tax system cites the 'absence of a harmonised addressing system' as a structural constraint, and academic geocoding research confirms there is no official address standard, with private ventures (e.g. NIMA Codes) attempting to fill the gap.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the business register?
Comments: Business formalization processes in Senegal commonly result in both RCCM registration and attribution of NINEA (national enterprise identifier) per reviewed references, indicating linkage between business registration and tax identification.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The original sources only established that NINEA exists alongside RCCM registration, supporting a cautious 'Under development' (3) score. Further checking (a specialist tax-procedure guide and the org-id.guide identifier directory, whose source is Senegal's own tax authority website) confirms that obtaining a NINEA is a standard, near-universal step within the business incorporation process, issued directly by the Direction Générale des Impôts et des Domaines (DGID) alongside RCCM registration — indicating an operational, not merely developing, linkage. Score raised from 3/Under development to 4/Partially integrated. Not raised to 5/Fully integrated nationwide, as no source confirms a fully unified, real-time technical link (e.g. shared database or API) across all business types and registers.
revised_comments: All businesses registering in Senegal must obtain a NINEA (Numéro d'Identification National des Entreprises et des Associations), issued by the tax authority (Direction Générale des Impôts et des Domaines) as a standard step in the incorporation process alongside RCCM commercial registration. This creates an operational link between business registration and the tax administration system, though there is no confirmed evidence of a fully unified, real-time technical integration across all registers nationwide.
